title: VPC Control Plane Security Kit: Terraform module for SGs, NACLs, Private DNS & Egress
creator: Marco Reyes
description: Build a reusable, versioned Terraform module (VPC Control Plane Security Kit) that encapsulates Redwood's recommended security posture for private deployments. The module will provision opinionated Security Groups and Network ACLs, manage private Route53 Resolver / Private DNS entries, and enforce egress controls (allowlists, egress proxy integration, and DNS egress resolution). It must include upgrade scripts and healthcheck tooling so infra teams can safely apply upgrades and detect drift or misconfigurations.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes inputs for: environment tag, allowed egress CIDR list, service security group sets, private-dns zone attachments, and egress-proxy endpoint
Module produces outputs for: security_group_ids, nacl_ids, resolver_rule_ids, and a semantic module version
Module has documented zero-downtime upgrade path with migration steps and example state transitions
Terraform plan/apply for a sample cluster (dev sandbox) results in no open inbound rules except approved bastion and load-balancer ports
Healthcheck job (Terraform null_resource + AWS Lambda or monitoring script) reports NACL mismatches, missing resolver rules, and unexpected outbound CIDRs
Automated CI validates module linting, unit tests (terratest), and applies module in an isolated account using ephemeral state
implementation_notes: Structure as a single root module with optional submodules: sg, nacl, dns_resolver, egress_policy
Use Terraform 1.5+ features and lock provider versions; support both S3+Dynamo state backend and remote state via remote backend wrapper
Provide a migration helper (Go tool or Terraform external data) that can detect existing permissive rules and generate a staged plan to tighten them with canary hosts
Encapsulate egress allowlist as a managed resource set with tagging so external auditors can query allowed egress for an account
Integrate with existing Egress Proxy (ENG-33108) by accepting proxy endpoints and toggles for forced-proxy tags on SGs
Private DNS: create conditional forwarders / resolver rules and ensure cross-account DNS associations use accepted delegation pattern
Healthchecks: implement a Lambda that runs daily and writes results to a Datadog metric + SNS alert for critical mismatches
Testing: terratest harness to create VPC, attach module, verify no '0.0.0.0/0' outbound where prohibited, verify resolver rules are attached
progress_updates: 2026-02-24: Kickoff meeting with Infra and Security. Agreed scope and non-goals (does not replace account-level guardrails).
2026-03-01: Prototype sg submodule complete; basic inputs and outputs wired. Initial terratest passes for port-level assertions.
2026-03-05: NACL design reviewed with Network team. Decided to make NACLs optional per-environment because managed firewalls exist for some customers.
2026-03-10: Private DNS approach chosen: use Route53 Resolver rules + association resources; need cross-account role for association automation.
2026-03-12: First draft PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/148 - awaiting code-review from @dmitri and @sara
review_feedback: Security: prefer deny-listing in NACLs only where high-risk subnets exist; otherwise use SGs for east-west controls
Platform: add opt-in feature flag for 'strict-egress' to allow gradual rollout across org
DevEx: include example usage and a small demo repository that spins up a test VPC with module applied
SRE: healthcheck Lambda should emit structured metrics and a runbook link for actionable alerts
risks: Applying strict egress by default in existing accounts could break services; mitigation: default to 'audit-only' mode and provide migration tooling
Cross-account resolver associations require IAM permissions that some customers cannot grant; mitigation: document manual steps and fallback patterns
State drift during module upgrade could leave orphaned security rules; mitigation: provide idempotent cleanup scripts and pre-flight dry-run tool
Terraform provider changes may cause churn across versions; mitigation: pin provider versions and document supported Terraform versions
test_plan: Unit: run tflint and checkov on module codebase
Integration: terratest suite creates ephemeral AWS account VPC, applies module, verifies SG/NACL/resolver resources
Upgrade test: run upgrade scenario from v0.1.0 -> v1.0.0 in CI with recorded state snapshots and validate no service interruption
Chaos: simulate a missing resolver rule and verify healthcheck alerts and automated remediation steps
Performance: measure plan/apply time and ensure it is acceptable for incremental runs (target < 5 minutes for small VPC)
